findings.evidence: `QuiverRep` is implemented as `Paths Q ⥤ ModuleCat k` in `Representation/Basic.lean:37`, while existing public vertexwise statements use `i : Q` with `((Paths.of Q).obj i)`, e.g. `DimensionVector.lean:79–80` and `Comparison.lean:149`; `Paths` itself is only a defined copy of its vertex type (`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/PathCategory/Basic.lean:32`).
findings.fix: In lines 81, 91, and 104–105 quantify over `a : Q` and use `f.app ((Paths.of Q).obj a)`; prove the internal all-`Paths Q` fact only locally if needed.
findings.issue: All three pointwise theorems quantify over `a : Paths Q`, although their advertised vertexwise API naturally quantifies over vertices `a : Q`; this leaks the free-category implementation and is inconsistent with nearby representation APIs.

summary: The categorical API is naturally general, but the quiver specialization exposes the implementation index `Paths Q` instead of the library’s vertex-level `Q` interface.
